source.note: Figures describe Val Thorens–Orelle (the resort's own pass). Search summary of valthorens.com and Val Thorens guide pages: 150 km of slopes; 85 runs = 12 green, 35 blue, 30 red, 8 black; 32 lifts including 10 gondolas and 13 chairlifts (the other 9, including the Cime Caron cable car and surface lifts, not broken down). Cime Caron cable car reopened for 2025-26 with two new 150-person cabins, 1,430 people/hour. Linked Les 3 Vallées area (official 'in figures' page, search summary): 600 km of pistes, 334 pistes (53 green, 136 blue, 108 red, 37 black), 161 lifts, of which the summary itemised 34 gondolas, 3 cable cars, 57 chairlifts and 33 drag lifts (the other 34 not broken down); Wikipedia puts total uplift at about 284,500 skiers/hour in 2026 (estimate).

character: Val Thorens, at about 2,300 m, is the highest resort in Les 3 Vallées and is linked with Orelle in the Maurienne valley (about 150 km of pistes on the Val Thorens–Orelle pass). The ski-in/ski-out village connects to Les Menuires, Méribel and Courchevel in the 600 km 3 Vallées area; the 2026-27 season runs from 21 Nov 2026 to 2 May 2027.
learning: Val Thorens–Orelle has 12 green and 35 blue runs (search summary). The high altitude makes it cold and exposed in mid-winter; reference: beginner areas are close to the village. Confirm beginner-lift access and lessons locally.

announcedOpening.text: Val Thorens and Orelle open 21 Nov 2026 and run to 2 May 2027 (France Montagnes 2026-27 list and Val Thorens day-pass price bands, per search summaries).

announcedClosing.text: Season to 2 May 2027 (per search summaries; day-pass price bands run to 2 May).

season.notes: Links to the rest of Les 3 Vallées depend on each valley's opening (Méribel 5 Dec 2026, Courchevel 4–5 Dec 2026, per search summaries). Past seasons were not captured.
